clue.text: One of cadet branch of the Forsyte lot, do we hear ?

definitions.text: One of cadet branch of the Forsyte lot, do we hear ?

parts.words: One of cadet branch of the Forsyte lot, do we hear
parts.note: a cadet branch is a junior line, so minor; 'Forsyte' said aloud is foresight, and the foresight lot are the seers of the Bible, here one of the lesser twelve

explanation.surface: A question about a junior member of the family in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forsyte Saga is John Galsworthy's novel sequence about a wealthy family. Said aloud 'Forsyte' is 'foresight', which seers have; a cadet (junior) branch of them is the minor ones, the twelve short books at the end of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve shorter books of Hosea to Malachi are attributed to the lesser seers, a junior line of biblical foretellers.

clue.text: Metallic flower gives copper a cheerful exterior

indicators.note: the cheerful word is given to copper as its outside, so it wraps round
the cheerful word is given to copper as its outside, so it wraps round

parts.note: cheerful means merry
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A shiny flower gives a policeman a happy outward look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a thing that flows: quicksilver is the liquid metal. 'Exterior' puts MERRY round CU; 'copper' might be a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is the only metal liquid at room temperature, so it flows: a metallic flower.

clue.text: Nick is not a man of honour

parts.note: taken as written
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick is said to lack honour.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order awarded for national service. 'Nick' looks like a man's name but means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove, a synonym.

clue.text: Remember to take the plate round again.

definitions.meaning: pass the collection plate in church a second time

explanation.surface: A reminder that the church collection must be taken a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the plate round is making a church collection; doing it again is re-collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To call back to mind is a synonym of remember, and gathering offerings a second time is to collect once more.

clue.text: Where gold is a 'currency unit

definitions.meaning: the Witwatersrand, South Africa's great gold-mining ridge, is called by its short name

explanation.surface: A question about where gold is a currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The Witwatersrand ridge near Johannesburg holds the world's largest gold deposits, and South Africa's currency is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: South Africa's gold-mining region shares its name with that country's money.

clue.text: "Her——han' she tried on man" (Burns)

parts.note: a gap to fill from Burns's song Green Grow the Rashes, O, where Nature makes man with her learner's hand before making women

explanation.surface: A quotation from Robert Burns with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns's song Green Grow the Rashes, O says Nature tried her apprentice hand on man, then made the lasses; 'prentice' is Scots-style short for apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots short form of apprentice, a learner, fills the gap in the Burns line.

clue.text: Put a bob in before you scrub

indicators.note: the pair of letters are put inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a bob was a shilling, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: Advice to pay a shilling before you clean something.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was British slang for a shilling, written S (from Latin solidus). 'In' puts A S inside ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel it, to wipe it out: a synonym.

clue.text: Where lewd fellows make the most of the bargains?

definitions.text: Where lewd fellows make the most of the bargains?

parts.words: Where lewd fellows make the most of the bargains
parts.note: lewd fellows are base men, and the cheapest sale floor of a department store is the bargain one

explanation.surface: A question about where lecherous men find the best deals.
explanation.walkthrough: Base men are lewd fellows; the 'bargain' floor of a department store is traditionally underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground floor of a building, in shops traditionally the bargain floor.

clue.text: Cat consumes article in Swiss Cottage

indicators.note: the cat swallows the article, so it goes inside

parts.note: chat is French for cat
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: A cat eating a piece in a Swiss Cottage, a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: French words, fitting Swiss: CHAT (cat) consumes LE (the). Swiss Cottage is also a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine wooden house with overhanging eaves is the typical Swiss cottage.

clue.text: Trouble centre needs icebreaker in reserve

indicators.note: ice is the thing that breaks in, so it is set inside the shuffled letters
to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of centre are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone shy needs something to break the ice at a busy centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' turns CENTRE into RETNCE, and 'breaker in' sends ICE into the middle of it: RET + ICE + NCE. 'Icebreaker' looks like one thing, a party game for the shy, but splits as ice plus breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in the sense of restraint in speech or manner is a synonym for keeping quiet.

clue.text: Jack Wood — for shame !

definitions.note: a verb here: to shame someone

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A man called Jack Wood is scolded for his conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack Wood' reads as a person's name but splits into sailor and timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone and to make them embarrassed or disconcerted are the same act; the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Said to be not entirely wicked ?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the made-up word for partly sounds like the solution

parts.note: not wholly, made into one word as un-wholly

explanation.surface: Someone is described as only partly bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' gives UN-WHOLLY, which spoken is the same as the word for sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irreligious and evil is profane, so wicked is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Note the genuine airy fairy

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G
genuine means real

explanation.surface: A comment that a fairy who flits through the air is the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy and fairy-like is delicate and insubstantial, light as heavenly vapour; a synonym.

clue.text: One tugged to the stadium-by the lure of baseball?

definitions.text: One tugged to the stadium-by the lure of baseball?

parts.words: One tugged to the stadium-by the lure of baseball
parts.note: a person yanked (tugged) is jokingly a ..., and the New York baseball team play at their own stadium

explanation.surface: A fan dragged to the ballpark because baseball is irresistible.
explanation.walkthrough: To yank is to tug, so one who is tugged is a 'yank-ee'; the New York Yankees are a baseball team with their own stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An American, especially a New Yorker, or a player for the New York baseball club, is called this.

clue.text: No picture-maker

definitions.meaning: the developed film from which photographic prints are made

explanation.surface: Someone who does not make pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusing reply is this kind of answer, and in photography the reversed-tone film used to print photos.

clue.text: The setting of a setting

parts.note: the place (setting) where the sun's going down (setting) takes place, that is, the west

explanation.surface: A phrase about the backdrop of a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'setting' means a location, the second the sun going down: where the sun sets is the west.
explanation.definitionFit: The western part of the world, where the sun goes down, is named from the Latin for falling.

clue.text: Caused by lack of food in an intoxicated Army hut?

definitions.text: Caused by lack of food in an intoxicated Army hut?

parts.words: Caused by lack of food in an intoxicated Army hut
parts.note: exhaustion from starvation, and also 'in a Nissen' said by a drunk who slurs it

explanation.surface: A soldier fainting from hunger in a barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nissen hut is a half-cylinder army hut; a drunk slurring 'in a Nissen' says something like 'in-a-nishun'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustion and weakness from want of nourishment is the medical sense of the word.

clue.text: A stretcher is needed for its use in attack

definitions.text: A stretcher is needed for its use in attack

parts.words: A stretcher is needed for its use in attack
parts.note: a stretcher here is the elastic band pulled taut to fling a stone, not a bed for the wounded

explanation.surface: Battlefield casualties need stretchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests carrying the wounded, but here it is the elastic that is stretched to fling a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A slingshot or siege engine that hurls missiles in war; both need stretched elastic or rope.

clue.text: One for the bed? How topping !

definitions.text: One for the bed? How topping !

parts.words: One for the bed? How topping
parts.note: a drink taken before sleep, and also headwear worn in bed, a topping for the head at night

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at the offer of a last drink before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One for the bed' is a last drink; 'topping' is both a delighted exclamation and something worn on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A final drink before sleep, or a soft cap once worn in bed, both go by this name.

clue.text: Novel flood precaution on the Trent

parts.note: novel means new
Noah built an ark before the Flood

explanation.surface: A new flood defence for the River Trent.
explanation.walkthrough: Newark-on-Trent is a market town in Nottinghamshire on the River Trent in the English Midlands. 'Novel' is an adjective here, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nottinghamshire town is officially Newark-on-Trent, so a place on that river.

clue.text: Start to chew gum

indicators.note: only the start of the word is kept, so its tail is cut off

parts.note: to masticate is to chew

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin chewing some gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to chew' means the start of MASTICATE, losing its last three letters ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from a Mediterranean tree, once chewed like chewing gum, and the word also names gummy adhesives.

clue.text: It cast light on strange secrets

indicators.note: strange means the letters of secrets are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something revealed strange secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges SECRETS. 'Cast light on' looks like 'revealed', but a cresset is a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron basket of burning fuel on a pole, used as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Tompion, the' vigilant

definitions.meaning: Thomas Tompion was a famous English maker of clocks and pocket timepieces
one who keeps guard at night

explanation.surface: Tompion described as ever alert.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tompion (1639-1713) was the most famous English clock- and watch-maker, so a 'watch man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of pocket timepieces could be styled this way, and a night guard who stays alert is the usual sense.

clue.text: The spring-board game

parts.note: a board game in which pieces jump (spring) over others, its name from the Greek for leap

explanation.surface: A game played on a diving board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring-board' suggests diving, but it is a board game of springing: pieces leap over each other, and the name is Greek for 'jump'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian game where pieces jump across a squared board to the opposite corner.

clue.text: But other hands are tinier

parts.note: on a clock the hand counting sixty seconds is the long one, while the others are shorter; the word also means tiny

explanation.surface: A remark that someone else's hands are smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on a clock face: the hand that marks sixty seconds is long, the other hands are smaller, yet its name as an adjective means very small.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means extremely small, and as a noun it names the long hand on a clock face.

clue.text: With unbowed head locks up the boy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: locks of the head are hair

explanation.surface: A proud boy with his head held high has his hair tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses HAIR to RIAH; 'unbowed head' is U, first letter of unbowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's given name from the Bible, borne by Dickens's Heep.

clue.text: Exalted disapproval of such reproduction?

parts.note: exalted means high and an expression of disapproval is fie, together sounding like the name of quality sound equipment

explanation.surface: Lofty scorn for a kind of copy.
explanation.walkthrough: High (exalted) plus fie (disapproval) sounds like the abbreviation for high fidelity sound reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for high fidelity, sound reproduction faithful to the original.

clue.text: This wild party goes back to the bar

indicators.note: going back means the word for a bar is read from right to left

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A rowdy party returns to the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes back to' turns LEVER round. 'The bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy, lively celebration is a carouse or spree, the noun sense of merrymaking.

clue.text: Monopoly's useful monopolies

definitions.meaning: in the board game Monopoly the Electric Company and Water Works are a pair of cards
services such as gas, water and electricity, each usually supplied by a single company

explanation.surface: A comment on the useful properties in the Monopoly board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is a board game of buying property; two of its squares are the Electric Company and Water Works.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monopoly cards for electricity and water carry this group name, as do public services like power and water supply.

clue.text: Arrow in flight

parts.note: an arrow loosed while running away, as ancient mounted archers of Persia did; flight means fleeing, not flying

explanation.surface: An arrow travelling through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' means fleeing: Parthian horse archers turned in the saddle to shoot as they retreated, so the phrase now means a cutting parting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Parthians fired arrows back while retreating, so the term names a missile loosed in retreat, and now a parting barb.
